**Generated by:** Idari (admin AI)  
**Source files read:** `docs/LAW.md`, `docs/AXIOMS.md`, `docs/IDARI_CONTRACT.md`,
`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/FEATURE_STATUS.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`,

**Authority:** `README.md` wins all naming conflicts (AXIOMS §Alignment rule)

---

## Executive Summary

Phase 1 established the canonical route skeleton, the four-layer Dream architecture,
and the AI triad endpoints. The system is structurally sound.

Phase 2 is a **naming and boundary alignment sprint**, not a rebuild. Every item
below targets one of the four priorities listed in `docs/FEATURE_STATUS.md §8`:

1. Make spec names primary everywhere in docs and UI copy
2. Continue folding legacy widget naming into Dreams naming
3. Tighten EditProfileDream → ViewProfile projection boundaries
4. Repurpose extra legacy routes into spec-defined systems

---

## Priority 1 — Make Spec Names Primary Everywhere in Docs and UI Copy

These are the highest-value, lowest-risk changes. Naming in UI copy carries the
product's identity — every wrong label trains the user (and AI context) to use the
old vocabulary.

---

### P1-A · `app/profile/[handle]/page.tsx`

**Current state — two problems in the same file:**

```tsx
// Line 82 — wrong label for the owner's own profile view
{isOwner ? 'My Profile' : `@${handle}`}

// Line 89 — links to legacy /edit-profile instead of canonical route
href="/edit-profile"
```

**Why this matters:** The owner visiting their own profile URL sees "My Profile"
as the page title. The spec calls this surface **ViewProfile** (README §6). The
owner is previewing their public output — the page should say "ViewProfile" or
"Your ViewProfile". Equally, the pencil edit button sends the owner to the legacy
support route `/edit-profile`, which just redirects — but the label in code and
any server-rendered link metadata will reflect the wrong route.

**Change required:**

```tsx
// Line 82
{isOwner ? 'ViewProfile' : `@${handle}`}

// Line 89 — change href to canonical route
href="/edit-profiledream"
```

## Priority 2 — Continue Folding Legacy Widget Naming into Dreams Naming

The four-layer Dream system (`DreamShell → DreamConnectorLayer → DreamFeatureLayer →
DreamOutputLayer`) is defined in `components/dreams/`. The problem is that
`DreamShell.tsx` is currently just a one-line pass-through to `WidgetShell`, and
the actual implementation lives under `components/widgets/WidgetShell.tsx` with
all the "Widget" vocabulary. Phase 2 should invert this relationship.

---

### P2-A · `components/dreams/DreamShell.tsx` — Invert the relationship

**Current state:**

```tsx
// components/dreams/DreamShell.tsx — current (3 lines total)
import WidgetShell, { type WidgetShellProps } from '@/components/widgets/WidgetShell';
export type DreamShellProps = WidgetShellProps;
export default function DreamShell(props: DreamShellProps) {
  return <WidgetShell {...props} />;
}
```

**Why this matters:** DreamShell is the canonical Layer 1 implementation per
`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §4`. But right now it's the thin wrapper — WidgetShell is
the real component. Every import of `WidgetShell` bypasses the Dream model entirely.
The `WidgetShellProps` type exported from `DreamShell` are actually `WidgetShellProps`
— the spec name is never the source of truth.

**Change required:**

Expand `DreamShell.tsx` to be the real implementation. Move the full body of
`WidgetShell.tsx` into `DreamShell.tsx`, replacing all internal references from
"Widget" to "Dream" in prop names, type names, and menu copy. Then make
`WidgetShell` the backward-compatible re-export:

```tsx
// components/widgets/WidgetShell.tsx — after migration
// Backward-compat shim. Prefer DreamShell directly.
export { default } from '@/components/dreams/DreamShell';
export type { DreamShellProps as WidgetShellProps } from '@/components/dreams/DreamShell';
```

Specific renames inside the moved implementation:

| Current (WidgetShell) | After (DreamShell) |
|---|---|
| `WidgetShellProps` | `DreamShellProps` |
| `WidgetErrorBoundary` | `DreamErrorBoundary` |
| `WidgetDataState` | `DreamDataState` |
| `data-widget-id` attribute | `data-dream-id` |
| `aria-label="Dream options"` | already correct — keep |
| `"Hide Dream"` menu item | already correct — keep |
| `"Remove Dream"` menu item | already correct — keep |
| `{title} could not load.` | keep |

The menu items already use Dream language — the component body is halfway there.
This change finishes the alignment.

### P2-B · `components/profile/ProfileWidgetGrid.tsx` — Type and export naming

**Current state (lines 10–58):**

```tsx
export type WidgetType = 'bio' | 'activity' | 'followers' | …
export type WidgetSize = 'small' | 'large';
export type WidgetBgStyle = 'white' | 'glass' | …
export type WidgetConfig = { accentColor: string; … }
export type Widget = { id: string; type: WidgetType; … }
export const DEFAULT_WIDGETS: Widget[] = […]
```

**Why this matters:** `ProfileWidgetGrid` is imported by both `EditProfileDream`
and `profile/[handle]/page.tsx`. Its exported types are the source of truth for
the profile layer's Dream objects. They're all named "Widget*". Any code that
imports these types learns the wrong vocabulary.

**Change required:**

Rename the exported types (keep the old names as deprecated re-exports for one
sprint to avoid breaking downstream):

```tsx
// Primary exports — new canonical names
export type DreamType = 'bio' | 'activity' | 'followers' | …
export type DreamSize = 'small' | 'large';
export type DreamBgStyle = 'white' | 'glass' | …
export type DreamConfig = { accentColor: string; … }
export type ProfileDream = { id: string; type: DreamType; … }
export const DEFAULT_DREAMS: ProfileDream[] = […]

// Backward-compat aliases — mark @deprecated
/** @deprecated Use DreamType */
export type WidgetType = DreamType;
/** @deprecated Use ProfileDream */
export type Widget = ProfileDream;
/** @deprecated Use DEFAULT_DREAMS */
export const DEFAULT_WIDGETS = DEFAULT_DREAMS;
```

## Priority 3 — Tighten EditProfileDream → ViewProfile Projection Boundaries

This is the most architecturally significant priority. The projection layer
(`lib/dreams/profileProjection.ts`, `components/dreams/DreamOutputLayer.tsx`)
exists but is not wired into the actual profile render path. `view-profile/page.tsx`
just redirects and `profile/[handle]/page.tsx` renders the same component whether
it's the owner editing or a visitor viewing.

---

### P3-A · `app/view-profile/page.tsx` — Make it a real page, not a redirect

**Current state:**

```tsx
// Entire file: just redirects to /profile/[handle]
export default async function ViewProfileAliasPage() {
  …redirect(`/profile/${profile.handle}`);
}
```

**Why this matters:** README §6.2 says "View Profile is a separate link available
from Edit ProfileDream so the user can preview before saving." README §6.4 says
the user must be able to "click View Profile, see the profile as a viewer would see
it, return to editing, save only when satisfied." A redirect to the generic profile
route collapses the distinction between the builder's preview and the public
destination. The page has no independent render or projection context.

**Change required:**

Replace the redirect with a real page render that:
1. Shows a "preview mode" banner to the owner — indicating they are in
   ViewProfile preview, not the live public view
2. Renders the profile using `DreamOutputLayer` so only visibility-approved
   content shows
3. Provides a "← Back to EditProfileDream" button and a "Looks good — Save & Publish" CTA

```tsx
// app/view-profile/page.tsx — new structure (server component)
export default async function ViewProfilePage() {
  const supabase = await createServerClient();
  const { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser();
  if (!user) redirect('/login');

  const { data: profile } = await supabase
    .from('profiles').select('*').eq('id', user.id).single();
  if (!profile?.handle) redirect('/edit-profiledream');

  // Fetch only the saved widget projection for this profile
  // (not raw HomeDream state — projection only)
  const savedWidgetOrder = …; // read from Supabase, not localStorage

  return (
    <ViewProfilePreview
      profile={profile}
      savedWidgets={savedWidgetOrder}
      isOwnerPreview   // shows the "preview mode" banner
    />
  );
}
```

The key behavioral difference from the current redirect: the owner sees a clear
preview context, not the same page a visitor would land on.

---

### P3-B · `app/edit-profiledream/page.tsx` — Move widget projection state to Supabase

**Current state (lines 53–58):**

```tsx
let loadedWidgets = DEFAULT_WIDGETS;
try {
  const saved = localStorage.getItem('de-profile-widget-order');
  if (saved) loadedWidgets = JSON.parse(saved);
} catch { /* noop */ }
```

**And on save (line 95):**

```tsx
localStorage.setItem('de-profile-widget-order', JSON.stringify(widgets));
```

**Why this matters:** Widget order and visibility for the profile are stored in
`localStorage`. This means:
- The projection state is device-bound — changing devices resets the profile layout
- The `/api/profile` PUT endpoint (line 76–91) saves bio/name/avatar but NOT widget
  arrangement
- ViewProfile and `/profile/[handle]` can never receive the saved widget order from
  the server — they will always render `DEFAULT_WIDGETS`
- This violates AXIOMS §Privacy by Design: the saved state that feeds the public
  output must be server-persisted, not browser-only

**Change required:**

1. Add a `profile_dream_widgets` column (JSONB) to the `profiles` Supabase table
   (new migration file: `supabase/migrations/YYYYMMDD_profile_dream_widgets.sql`)
2. In `edit-profiledream/page.tsx`: load widget order from `profile.profile_dream_widgets`
   instead of `localStorage`
3. In `handleSave`: include `widget_order: widgets` in the `PUT /api/profile` body
4. In `app/api/profile/route.ts`: persist `widget_order` to `profile_dream_widgets`
5. In `app/profile/[handle]/page.tsx` and the new `view-profile/page.tsx`:
   read widget order from `profile.profile_dream_widgets`

Migration stub:

```sql
-- supabase/migrations/YYYYMMDD_profile_dream_widgets.sql
ALTER TABLE profiles
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS profile_dream_widgets JSONB DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb;

COMMENT ON COLUMN profiles.profile_dream_widgets IS
  'Saved projection — the ordered list of Dreams the user has chosen to show on ViewProfile.
   This is the output of EditProfileDream, not HomeDream source state.';
```

---

### P3-C · `app/profile/[handle]/page.tsx` — Separate owner-preview from public visitor render

**Current state:** A single page component with an `isOwner` boolean that only
changes one `<h1>` label and toggles the edit pencil button. No projection filtering.
The same `ProfileWidgetGrid` with the same `DEFAULT_WIDGETS` renders for both.

**Why this matters:** README §6.3 states ViewProfile "must show only explicitly
allowed public/shared content" and "never expose private HomeDream content."
README §5.3 states "no private HomeDream content appears publicly without explicit
user action." With the current implementation, all default widgets render for all
visitors — there is no visibility enforcement.

**Change required (two-part):**

**Part 1 — Owner path:** When `isOwner === true`, render a banner linking to
EditProfileDream and redirect notice:

```tsx
{isOwner && (
  <div style={{ … banner style … }}>
    <span>You are viewing your public ViewProfile.</span>
    <Link href="/edit-profiledream">Edit in EditProfileDream →</Link>
  </div>
)}
```

**Part 2 — Projection filtering:** Pass each widget through `DreamOutputLayer`
before rendering. Currently `DreamOutputLayer.tsx` exists and is correct in
isolation, but is never invoked in the profile render path.

```tsx
// In app/profile/[handle]/page.tsx or ProfileWidgetGrid
import DreamOutputLayer from '@/components/dreams/DreamOutputLayer';

// Wrap each widget render:
<DreamOutputLayer
  mode="profile"
  visibility={widget.visibility ?? 'private'}
  isExplicitlyShared={widget.isShared ?? false}
>
  <WidgetCard widget={widget} isEditing={false} />
</DreamOutputLayer>
```

This ensures widgets with `visibility: 'private'` or `isShared: false` are not
rendered on the public profile — matching the README §6.3 requirement.

---

### P3-D · `lib/dreams/profileProjection.ts` and `components/dreams/DreamOutputLayer.tsx` — Unify

**Current state:** Two parallel implementations of the same projection logic:

- `lib/dreams/profileProjection.ts` exports `canRenderProjection(projection, explicitShare)`
- `components/dreams/DreamOutputLayer.tsx` implements its own `canRender` inline:
  `const canRender = visibility !== 'private' && isExplicitlyShared`

**Why this matters:** Both check the same condition. The utility in `lib/` is never
called by the component in `components/`. If the projection rule ever changes, it
must be changed in two places. This will diverge.

**Change required:**

Import and use `canRenderProjection` from `lib/dreams/profileProjection.ts` inside
`DreamOutputLayer.tsx`:

```tsx
// components/dreams/DreamOutputLayer.tsx
import { canRenderProjection } from '@/lib/dreams/profileProjection';

export default function DreamOutputLayer({ mode, visibility, isExplicitlyShared, children }) {
  if (mode === 'profile') {
    const canRender = canRenderProjection(
      { widgetId: '', visibility: visibility ?? 'private', exposedFields: [] },
      isExplicitlyShared ?? false
    );
    return canRender ? <>{children}</> : null;
  }
  return <>{children}</>;
}
```

One source of truth for projection decisions.

## Priority 4 — Repurpose Extra Legacy Routes into Spec-Defined Systems

The three extra daydream routes (`analytics`, `media-vault`, `play`) are not in the
canonical six-pair list. The spec is explicit: there are exactly six Daydream/Engin
pairs (README §7.2). These routes must be mapped into the spec, not treated as
additional product surfaces.

---

### P4-A · `app/daydream/analytics/page.tsx` → redirect to BrandingEngin

**Current state:** Standalone page with `enginName="AnalyticsEngin"`. "AnalyticsEngin"
is not a canonical Engin name — it does not exist in README §7.2.

**Why this matters:** README §12.2 defines BrandingEngin (Side B of Brand Daydream)
as the home for "performance views", "audience or campaign system logic", and
"optimization flows". Analytics belongs inside BrandingEngin. Having a separate
`/daydream/analytics` route with its own "AnalyticsEngin" name creates a
non-canonical seventh pair.

**Change required:**

Replace the page body with a redirect to `/daydream/brand` plus a note:

```tsx
// app/daydream/analytics/page.tsx
import { redirect } from 'next/navigation';
export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic';
export default function AnalyticsDaydreamLegacyPage() {
  // Analytics is part of BrandingEngin (README §12.2 — performance views,
  // optimization flows). Redirect to Brand Daydream.
  redirect('/daydream/brand');
}
```

The existing content (post count metric, revenue section, connectors) should be
integrated into `app/daydream/brand/page.tsx` as a "BrandingEngin Analytics" Dream
widget panel on the Side B (Engin) surface.

---

### P4-B · `app/daydream/media-vault/page.tsx` → redirect to Create Daydream

**Current state:** Standalone page with `enginName="MediaEngin"`. "MediaEngin"
is not a canonical Engin name.

**Why this matters:** README §13.1 defines Create Daydream as the home for
"media composition", "mixed-content authoring", and "post/project development".
Media storage and file management are part of ContentEngin (Side B of Create
Daydream). Having a separate `/daydream/media-vault` with its own "MediaEngin"
label creates a non-canonical route.

**Change required:**

```tsx
// app/daydream/media-vault/page.tsx
import { redirect } from 'next/navigation';
export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic';
export default function MediaVaultLegacyPage() {
  // Media Vault is part of ContentEngin (README §13 — media composition,
  // mixed-content authoring). Redirect to Create Daydream.
  redirect('/daydream/create');
}
```

The existing content (upload CTA, media categories) should be integrated into
`app/daydream/create/page.tsx` as a "Media Library" Dream within ContentEngin's
Side B surface.

---

### P4-C · `app/daydream/play/page.tsx` → redirect to Music Daydream

**Current state:** Standalone page with `enginName="PlayEngin"`. "PlayEngin"
is not a canonical Engin name.

**Why this matters:** README §8.1 defines Music Daydream as the home for
"music creation, organization, upload, listening, managing projects, songs, drafts,
and audio assets." Playing/listening to music is a core Music Daydream function.
"Play" as a separate surface fragments what should live inside Music Daydream /
StarMakerEngin.

**Change required:**

```tsx
// app/daydream/play/page.tsx
import { redirect } from 'next/navigation';
export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic';
export default function PlayDaydreamLegacyPage() {
  // Play/listening is part of Music Daydream / StarMakerEngin (README §8.1).
  // Redirect to Music Daydream.
  redirect('/daydream/music');
}
```

The "Now Playing" widget, "Saved Music", and "Saved Videos" panels from the play
page should be integrated into `app/daydream/music/page.tsx` as Dream modules.

### P4-D · `app/api/dr-eams/hf/route.ts` and `app/api/dr-eams/run/route.ts` → mark as legacy, redirect

**Current state:** Two route files exist at `/api/dr-eams/hf` and `/api/dr-eams/run`.
The canonical endpoint is `/api/ai/eams` (per ARCHITECTURE.md, AGENT_PLAYBOOK.md).

**Why this matters:** `docs/BUGS.md` and `docs/FEATURE_STATUS.md §5` explicitly
list "legacy `/api/dr-eams/*` routes remain" as an open alignment gap. The canonical
route is `/api/ai/eams`. Having two active endpoints for Dr. Eams creates routing
ambiguity and risks calls being split between the legacy and canonical endpoints.

**Change required:**

Replace both route bodies with 301 redirects to the canonical endpoint:

```ts
// app/api/dr-eams/run/route.ts
import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';
export async function POST(req: NextRequest) {
  // Legacy route — canonical endpoint is /api/ai/eams
  return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/api/ai/eams', req.url), 301);
}
```

```ts
// app/api/dr-eams/hf/route.ts
import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';
export async function POST(req: NextRequest) {
  return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/api/ai/eams', req.url), 301);
}
```

---

### P4-E · `app/analytics/page.tsx` → redirect to BrandingEngin

**Current state:** A top-level `/analytics` route exists outside the Daydream
system. It duplicates the same content as `/daydream/analytics`.

**Why this matters:** Two separate analytics surfaces at `/analytics` and
`/daydream/analytics` both survive independently. Neither is a canonical spec route.
Both should resolve to BrandingEngin at `/daydream/brand`.

**Change required:**

```tsx
// app/analytics/page.tsx
import { redirect } from 'next/navigation';
export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic';
export default function AnalyticsLegacyPage() {
  redirect('/daydream/brand');
}
```

---

## What Phase 2 Does NOT Change

To be explicit about scope:

- No routes are deleted. All changed routes either redirect correctly or remain in
  place as support routes (per ARCHITECTURE.md §2).
- No auth or RLS logic is touched.
- No AI triad behavior changes.
- `docs/` files are not modified (read-only per Idari contract).
- `lib/ai/boogieman.ts` is not modified (governance file).
- The six canonical Daydream pages (`music`, `games`, `lab`, `code`, `brand`, `create`)
  are not changed — they are already correct.
- `DreamConnectorLayer.tsx`, `DreamFeatureLayer.tsx` — unchanged, already aligned.
